A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that the septum is not the only cause of the obstruction, and the mitral valve also has a major role.
we are not able to identify the exact pathophysiological mechanism of the obstruction.
we found that alcohol septal ablation is a safe and effective treatment for patients with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need a better understanding of the natural history of HCM and the pathophysiology of LVOT obstruction, as well as the long-term effects of the different treatment modalities.
the surgical approach to HCM is not a panacea for all HCM patients, and it should be reserved for patients with severe symptoms and/or a high risk of sudden death.
the LVOT gradient is not the most important determinant of outcome.
